record.what_it_does: Sentry is an application monitoring platform that provides a web API for programmatically managing organizations, projects, issues, releases, and error/performance data.
record.auth_notes: OAuth2 (authorization code grant + PKCE, plus a device authorization flow) is documented for third-party apps acting on behalf of users and is what the official MCP server uses. Personal 'user auth tokens' / internal-integration tokens are used as static Bearer tokens. Legacy API keys use HTTP Basic auth (username=key, empty password) and are disabled for new accounts. DSN-based auth is a limited, endpoint-specific static-key scheme.
record.access_notes: Anyone can sign up for Sentry's free 'developer' plan, which explicitly includes 'MCP access', and can create personal auth tokens or an OAuth app immediately per the auth docs, with no plan gate mentioned. However, Sentry's own pricing page lists 'API & third-party integrations' as a feature added starting at the paid Team plan ($26/mo), which introduces ambiguity about how much of the REST API/integration platform is usable on the free tier vs. requiring a paid plan.
record.main_blocker: Ambiguity/possible gating of full API & integration access behind the paid Team plan ($26/mo) per Sentry's pricing page
